questions.q: What is the core purpose-difference between a scratch org and a sandbox, per this lesson?
options: Scratch orgs are disposable and meant to be thrown away; sandboxes are long-lived and shared by a team
Sandboxes are disposable; scratch orgs are long-lived
There is no real difference — they're two names for the same thing
Scratch orgs can only be used for reporting, never for development
questions.explain: A scratch org is created on demand and meant to be deleted when done, starting fresh each time from a definition file; a sandbox is a long-lived copy of production that a team shares and maintains over time.

questions.q: Which three flags on `sf org create scratch` are mutually exclusive with each other, representing three of the four creation methods?
questions.explain: --edition, --snapshot, and --source-org are mutually exclusive with each other, representing three of the four ways to create a scratch org (the fourth being a definition file, which can be combined with these in some cases like the sourceOrg property).

questions.q: What is the valid range and default value for the `--duration-days` flag on scratch org creation?
questions.explain: A scratch org can be set to last anywhere from 1 to 30 days, and if you don't specify --duration-days, it defaults to 7 days.

questions.q: What happens when a scratch org expires?
options: It automatically converts into a sandbox
It's gone permanently — there's no way to extend or recover an already-expired scratch org
It pauses and can be resumed later with sf org resume scratch
Its data gets archived to the Dev Hub automatically
questions.explain: Scratch org expiration is final: once expired, the org and its contents are gone, with no extension or recovery path — a deliberate design choice that reinforces treating scratch orgs as disposable.

questions.q: Which command deletes a scratch org before its natural expiration, without an interactive confirmation prompt?
questions.explain: sf org delete scratch with --target-org specifying the org and --no-prompt skipping the confirmation prompt deletes a scratch org early, before it would otherwise expire on its own.
